# EGFR Kinase Target Brief

## Target Overview

**EGFR** (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor, also known as ErbB1/HER1) is a receptor tyrosine kinase encoded by the **EGFR gene** (chromosome 7p11.2) in humans.

- **UniProt ID:** P00533 (human EGFR)
- **Gene family:** ErbB/HER family of receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR/HER1, HER2/ErbB2, HER3/ErbB3, HER4/ErbB4)
- **Domain architecture:** Extracellular ligand-binding domain (binds EGF, TGF-α, amphiregulin, and other ligands) → single transmembrane helix → intracellular tyrosine kinase domain → C-terminal regulatory tail with autophosphorylation sites

**Biology:** Ligand binding induces receptor dimerization (homo- or heterodimerization with other ErbB members), activating the intracellular kinase domain via trans-autophosphorylation of tyrosine residues. This triggers downstream signaling through RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK, PI3K/AKT, and JAK/STAT pathways, driving cell proliferation, survival, and migration.

**Disease relevance:**
- Overexpression/amplification and activating mutations (e.g., **L858R**, **exon 19 deletions**, **T790M** gatekeeper resistance mutation, **C797S** third-generation resistance mutation) are major drivers in **non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)**
- Also implicated in glioblastoma (EGFRvIII variant), colorectal cancer, and head & neck squamous cell carcinoma
- One of the most clinically validated oncology drug targets, with multiple generations of approved inhibitors

## Known Structures (PDB)

EGFR kinase domain is one of the most extensively crystallized kinases — hundreds of structures exist. Representative/landmark entries:

| PDB ID | Description |
|---|---|
| **1M17** | EGFR kinase domain with erlotinib (first EGFR–inhibitor complex) |
| **2ITY / 2ITZ** | T790M gatekeeper mutant structures |
| **3W2S / 2ITO** | L858R activating mutant |
| **4LRM** | Osimertinib-bound (AZD9291), active against T790M |
| **5CAV** | EGFR with osimertinib, L858R/T790M double mutant |
| **1IVO** | Extracellular domain, ligand-bound dimer |
| **2J6M** | Inactive (apo) kinase conformation |

# EGFR Kinase Target Brief

## What Is Known

**Identity:** EGFR (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor), UniProt [P00533](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00533) (EGFR_HUMAN), gene *EGFR*, 1210 amino acids, human (*Homo sapiens*).

**Biology:** EGFR is a receptor tyrosine kinase of the ErbB/HER family (HER1). It consists of an extracellular ligand-binding region (binds EGF, TGF-α, and related ligands), a single transmembrane helix, and an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain. Ligand binding drives receptor dimerization (homo- or hetero-dimerization with HER2/ERBB2, HER3/ERBB4) and trans-autophosphorylation of C-terminal tyrosines, triggering downstream RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK and PI3K–AKT signaling that controls cell proliferation, survival, and differentiation.

**Disease relevance:** EGFR is one of the most important oncology drug targets. Activating mutations (e.g., L858R, exon 19 deletions) and amplification drive non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC); EGFR is also overexpressed in colorectal, head & neck, and other epithelial cancers. It is a validated target for both small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and monoclonal antibodies (e.g., cetuximab).

In ChEMBL, this maps to several related target entries, the primary one being the single-protein target **CHEMBL203** (Epidermal growth factor receptor, *H. sapiens*), plus family/combination entries such as CHEMBL2111431 (EGFR + ErbB2) and CHEMBL2363049 (broader ErbB family).

## Structures

EGFR's intracellular kinase domain is extensively structurally characterized — it was one of the first RTK kinase domains solved and remains among the most crystallized kinases, with structures covering:
- Apo and ATP/analog-bound kinase domain
- Active and inactive (autoinhibited) conformational states
- Complexes with essentially all approved EGFR TKIs (gefitinib, erlotinib, afatinib, osimertinib, lapatinib, etc.)
- Clinically relevant resistance mutants (e.g., T790M, L858R, exon 19 deletions, C797S)
- The extracellular dimerization domain bound to EGF-family ligands
